00:00 to 31:00, one oil-change visit Sample visit

Six stations. One clock.

Every job has a posted time. Here is a typical wait-for-it visit, split by station, so you know where your car is while you sit.

31:00

Lap 6 of 6, hand-back, 31 minutes in

  1. Check-in

    Keys, mileage and what you want done, written on the ticket. Wait with it or walk for a coffee.

    2 min02:00

  2. Oil

    Old oil drained, new filter on, filled with the oil your manual calls for, level checked twice.

    18 min20:00

  3. Filters

    Engine and cabin filters pulled and held up next to new ones. If they can wait, we say so.

    4 min24:00

  4. Tires

    Pressures set to the door sticker, tread read with a gauge, lugs looked over.

    3 min27:00

  5. Check

    Wipers, bulbs, belts and fluid levels looked at. Nothing gets swapped without your yes.

    3 min30:00

  6. Hand-back

    Keys back with a short report: what was done, what wasn’t due, and the mileage when it will be.

    Keys back

At 20:00: the oil goes in

Which oil does your car need?

The one your owner’s manual names. Here is how the three types differ, in plain words.

Type Conventional Synthetic blend Full synthetic
How often Shortest; your manual sets it In between Longest the manual allows
Cold mornings Thicker at start-up Flows better Flows fastest on an inversion morning
Older engines Fine when it’s the spec A common middle choice Holds up longer under heat
When we pour it The manual says conventional The manual allows either The manual calls for synthetic

We read the spec off your manual or the oil cap. No upsell to a better bottle.
